findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the step-3 discovery reference: the completion precheck's _referencing_commit_exists returns only a boolean (no SHAs); name completion_prefetch.referencing_commit_diffs (or specify the new SHA-collecting scan) as the actual reuse basis so trailer/subject parsing and descendant-id acceptance are not re-implemented divergently.
evidence: close_precheck.py:94-122 _referencing_commit_exists returns bool, iterates message bodies, `return True` on first match — no SHA list
completion_prefetch.py:284 referencing_commit_diffs collects `--format=%H` SHAs and shells `git show` per SHA
Plan: '(ii) the referencing-commit scan the close gate's completion precheck already performs ... commits reachable from the worktree HEAD carrying a rebar-ticket: trailer'
findings.finding: Step 3 states the DET commit set reuses 'the referencing-commit scan the close gate's completion precheck already performs', but that scan (_referencing_commit_exists) is a boolean over `git log --format=%B` message bodies that short-circuits on first match and collects NO commit SHAs, so it cannot be used as-is to feed `git show --name-only`; the closer reusable helper is completion_prefetch.referencing_commit_diffs, which does collect SHAs.
scenarios: Implementer tries to call/extend the boolean precheck scan and finds it emits no SHAs, or duplicates trailer-parsing logic instead of reusing the SHA-collecting prefetch helper

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct step 3's commit-discovery source (ii): the cited close-precheck scan (`_referencing_commit_exists`) returns a bool over commit messages, not a SHA list — specify a new SHA-enumerating scan (or extract from the existing bool seam / reuse `completion_prefetch.referencing_commit_diffs` which already emits %H).
evidence: Plan: 'the referencing-commit scan the close gate's completion precheck already performs (commits reachable from the worktree HEAD carrying a rebar-ticket: trailer...)' — then 'For each discovered commit, collect git show --name-only changed paths'

src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:94 `def _referencing_commit_exists(accepted_ids, tracker, repo_root) -> bool:` uses `git log --format=%B%x00` (commit BODIES only, no %H) and early-returns True on first match — it yields no SHA list
A separate helper src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_prefetch.py:284 `referencing_commit_diffs` DOES emit %H and run per-commit `git show`, but the plan cites the close-precheck scan, not this one
findings.finding: Step 3 asserts reuse of the close gate's existing referencing-commit scan as a per-commit SHA source, but that seam (_referencing_commit_exists) returns only a boolean and never enumerates SHAs — the capability the plan depends on does not exist in the form claimed.
scenarios: Implementer wires step 3 to _referencing_commit_exists and discovers it cannot yield the SHAs the file-impact-vs-diff check iterates over
findings.suggested_fix: Name the concrete SHA source: either refactor `_referencing_commit_exists` to return the matching SHAs (git log --format='%H%x00%B'), or reuse `completion_prefetch.referencing_commit_diffs`'s %H enumeration, and state that the file-impact check iterates that SHA list plus state.commits.

findings.finding: The DET close check specifies collecting changed paths via `git show --name-only` but does not define behavior for merge commits, where `git show --name-only` produces no per-file diff by default — a merge in the discovered commit set could either silently pass or behave unpredictably.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to step 3: 'merge commits are enumerated with `--first-parent` (or skipped); non-merge commits use `git show --name-only`.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the transition impact of the new close BLOCK on in-flight tickets and confirm the intended remedy (update file_impact / add exemption) is the only path, or note an explicit back-out.
evidence: 'a changed path that is neither within the recorded file_impact nor matched by this feature's OWN exemption globs ... is a deterministic close BLOCK'
The plan only preserves prior behavior for the no-commits and no-file_impact cases: 'A ticket with no discovered commits keeps today's behavior ... a ticket without file_impact is out of scope'
findings.finding: The DET close check introduces a new deterministic close BLOCK condition that can block tickets which are closable today (those with recorded file_impact AND discovered commits touching out-of-impact, non-exempt paths). This tightens the close gate's behavior for existing in-flight tickets, but the plan states no back-out/opt-out path or acknowledgement of the transition impact on tickets already in flight.
scenarios: An in-flight ticket with file_impact and a linked commit that legitimately touched an undeclared path is suddenly blocked at close after this change ships
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to step 3 acknowledging that the new check tightens close behavior and that the author's remedy is to correct file_impact (or that the exemption globs cover the common cases), confirming no back-out flag is warranted for this deterministic gate.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify why step 3's exemption-glob set is defined fresh rather than reusing/extending an existing file_impact-path classifier (e.g. orchestrator.bug_blast_radius_escalates), or note the intended divergence (tests/** vs tests/+conftest.py) explicitly so the choice is deliberate.
evidence: Plan quote: "matched by this feature's OWN exemption globs (tests/**, docs/**, **/*.md, CHANGELOG.md — defined and documented here, not inherited from any other gate)"
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:191-211 bug_blast_radius_escalates already classifies file_impact paths as test vs non-test (tests/ + conftest.py)
src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json:61 'docs/**' and reviewers/index.json:73 'tests/**' are existing exemption/scope glob conventions
The plan's tests/** vs the existing tests/ + conftest.py rule are not identical, so an unexplained new list risks silent divergence
findings.finding: Step 3 defines a brand-new, standalone exemption-glob list (tests/**, docs/**, **/*.md, CHANGELOG.md) declared 'not inherited from any other gate', but the codebase already contains at least one deterministic file_impact-path classifier (rebar.llm.plan_review.orchestrator.bug_blast_radius_escalates, which classifies tests/ and conftest.py) and several other exemption conventions (criteria_routing.json's docs/**, reviewer applies_to globs). The plan asserts semantic independence but does not justify why a fourth divergent exemption convention is preferable to reusing or extending an existing path classifier, risking convention drift (e.g. this list exempts all of tests/** but the blast-radius classifier's test rule is tests/ + conftest.py).
findings.location: Plan step 3 ('exemption globs (tests/**, docs/**, **/*.md, CHANGELOG.md) — defined and documented here, not inherited from any other gate)')
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer expects the diff-vs-impact exemptions to match the blast-radius test-path rule and is surprised by the divergence
conftest.py at repo root (not under tests/) is exempt in the blast-radius classifier but NOT by this feature's tests/** glob

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify (and bound the false-positive blast radius of) the touched-but-undeclared→BLOCK polarity in step 3: address commits that span multiple rebar-ticket: tickets and incidental non-exempt edits, or downgrade to advisory / narrow the block condition, since file_impact is a forward declaration that need not enumerate every landed path.
evidence: Plan: 'a changed path that is neither within the recorded file_impact nor matched by this feature's OWN exemption globs ... is a deterministic close BLOCK'
completion_prefetch.py:284 referencing_commit_diffs / assemble.py:274: a commit's rebar-ticket: trailer can name multiple tickets (union scope), so one commit's diff touches several tickets' files
file_impact is forward-declared (field_reads.file_impact, close_precheck.py:267) and is not guaranteed to enumerate every incidentally-touched path
findings.finding: The DET check blocks close whenever a discovered commit touches any path outside the declared file_impact, but file_impact is an author-declared forward declaration that is frequently coarser/narrower than the landed diff, and a single referencing commit legitimately spans multiple tickets (the code-review scope-intent overlay explicitly supports multiple rebar-ticket: trailers per commit) or carries incidental edits — so conforming work can be spuriously BLOCKED and the exemption globs (tests/**, docs/**, **/*.md) do not cover incidental src/ helpers or a co-referenced sibling ticket's files.
scenarios: A commit resolving two sibling tickets touches ticket B's file_impact paths while closing ticket A — A's file_impact does not list B's paths → spurious BLOCK
A commit that also touches an incidental src/ helper not enumerated in file_impact → spurious BLOCK on a legitimate close

findings.finding: SHA validation is placed only in the CLI verb (step 1), but the shared `rebar.attach_commits` seam performs no SHA validation, so the MCP tool and Python library — which step 2/AC#2 say route through the SAME seam — will not reject invalid SHAs, making the 'invalid SHAs are rejected' guarantee surface-specific rather than uniform across the three named surfaces.
findings.location: Plan step 1 vs step 2 / AC #1, AC #2; src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:697-724
findings.suggested_fix: Move 'validate each SHA resolves in the repo' from the CLI wrapper into the `rebar.attach_commits` seam so CLI, library, and MCP all reject invalid SHAs through the single seam.

findings.finding: SHA validation ('validate each SHA resolves in the repo') is placed in the CLI verb wrapper (step 1) rather than in the shared `attach_commits` engine seam, so the MCP `attach_commits` tool and the `rebar.attach_commits` library facade can record a COMMITS event with an unresolvable SHA.
findings.location: Plan step 1: 'CLI verb `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>...` wrapping the existing `rebar.attach_commits` seam (validate each SHA resolves in the repo; union-add semantics unchanged).'
findings.suggested_fix: State in step 1/2 that SHA-resolution validation lives in `attach_commits` core (the shared seam), with the CLI/MCP/library layers doing only parsing and error formatting on top; keep AC line 1's test exercising the seam directly.

findings.finding: Step 3 does not define the path-matching semantics for 'a changed path neither within the recorded file_impact'. file_impact entries are author-declared and can be coarse (a directory or module prefix), so an exact-equality interpretation would deterministically BLOCK conforming closes whenever a declared directory contains the changed file.
findings.location: Plan step 3 (DET close check) / AC line 3
findings.suggested_fix: State: a changed path is treated as in-impact when it equals a declared file_impact path OR is contained under a declared path treated as a directory/prefix; only paths matching neither impact nor the exemption globs block.

findings.finding: A new `attach-commits` CLI verb requires registration in the CLI dispatch partitions and a per-verb help file, but step 1 enumerates neither — these are consumers outside the docs the plan names.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to step 1: register the verb in the appropriate `_cli/__init__.py` dispatch frozenset (following set-file-impact) and add the matching help/attach-commits.txt and overview.txt line.

findings.finding: Step 1 places the new SHA-resolution validation ('validate each SHA resolves in the repo') inside the CLI verb, but Steps 1-2 say the library re-export and MCP tool route through the same `rebar.attach_commits` seam. If the SHA-resolves check lives only in the CLI wrapper rather than in the shared `attach_commits` seam/reducer, the library and MCP ingress paths can record a COMMITS event referencing a non-resolvable SHA, bypassing the guard.
findings.location: Step 1: 'CLI verb rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>... wrapping the existing rebar.attach_commits seam (validate each SHA resolves in the repo ...)'
findings.suggested_fix: Move the per-SHA resolution check into the `attach_commits` core/seam so all three surfaces reject unresolvable SHAs identically; keep only error-message formatting in the CLI/MCP layers.
